gloss: to be startled; to have a sudden realization

forms.label: Past polite
forms.negative: ハッとしませんでした

forms.label: ている past
forms.negative: ハッとしていなかった

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: ハッとしていませんでした

definitions.gloss: to be startled; to be taken aback
definitions.explanation: To be suddenly surprised or startled by something unexpected.

definitions.gloss: to suddenly realize; to have a moment of clarity
definitions.explanation: To have a sudden realization or awareness about something.

examples.japanese: {後|うし}ろから{声|こえ}をかけられてハッとした。
examples.english: I was startled when someone called out to me from behind.

examples.japanese: {鏡|かがみ}に{映|うつ}った{自分|じぶん}の{顔|かお}を{見|み}てハッとした。
examples.english: I was taken aback when I saw my own face in the mirror.

examples.japanese: {車|くるま}が{急|きゅう}に{飛|と}び{出|だ}してきて、ハッとして{急|きゅう}ブレーキを{踏|ふ}んだ。
examples.english: A car suddenly darted out, and I was so startled that I slammed on the brakes.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{一言|ひとこと}でハッとした。
examples.english: His words gave me a sudden realization.

examples.japanese: {忘|わす}れ{物|もの}に{気|き}づいてハッとした。
examples.english: I suddenly realized I'd forgotten something.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}の{素直|すなお}な{質問|しつもん}にハッとさせられることがある。
examples.english: Children's honest questions sometimes make you stop and think.

notes:
USAGE:
ハッとする uses the mimetic ハッ (a sudden, sharp sensation) with する. It describes a split-second experience — either being startled or having a flash of insight. The katakana spelling ハッ is standard.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ハッとする: to be startled / to suddenly realize
- ハッとさせられる: to be made to stop and think
- ハッとした{表情|ひょうじょう}: a startled expression
- ハッと{気|き}づく: to suddenly notice

SIMILAR WORDS:
びっくりする is a more general word for being surprised. ハッとする emphasizes the sharp, instantaneous quality of the surprise or realization.
